statement.p: Find the Jacobian. \frac{\partial (x,y,z)}{\partial (s,t,u)}, where x = 4u-\left(s+2t\right), y = 4s+t+5u, z = 3u-\left(2s+2t\right).

static.solution: \left|\frac{\partial (x,y,z)}{\partial (s,t,u)}\right| = \left|\begin{array}{ccc} x_s \amp x_t \amp x_u\\ y_s \amp y_t \amp y_u\\ z_s \amp z_t \amp z_u \end{array}\right| =\left|\begin{array}{ccc} -1 \amp -2 \amp 4\\ 4 \amp 1 \amp 5\\ -2 \amp -2 \amp 3 \end{array}\right|. This 3 \times 3 determinant is computed the same way as for the cross product, with the entries -1,-2,4 in the first row playing the same role as \vec i,\vec j,\vec k. We get \frac{\partial (x,y,z)}{\partial (s,t,u)}= ((1)(3)-(5)(-2))-1 + ((5)(-2)-(4)(3))-2 + ((4)(-2)-(1)(-2))4 = 7.
